question: Do the Hecate regional outputs and resource benefits repeat in a clean environment, including a correctly selected surrounding-context crop as a competitive baseline?
baseline: Unmodified pinned Hecate full-field prediction. Stronger alternative: independently enumerate the full-grid tiles intersecting the requested ROI, crop their bounding context, run unmodified Hecate, then crop its output. All methods use CPU fp32,batch1,default stride and unchanged weights.
comparison: Existing frozen regional API, three balanced-order repeats per case/region; two fine-resolution central cases and edge/centre/large requests on three coarse-resolution specimens. No new algorithm fitting.
metric: Every saved output value against corresponding full-field prediction; repeat equality; model calls; exact temporary accumulator bytes; paired full/ROI and halo/ROI time ratios, median/min/max of three repetitions. No pixel-independence or hardware-population confidence interval.
success_condition: All regional and correctly cropped-context outputs match full-field outputs exactly in every repeat. Median paired full/ROI speedup >=1.5 in both fine central cases and all three coarse central cases. For small requests, regional temporary arrays at least16x smaller than context-crop arrays and median ROI/context-crop runtime <=1.25. Large requests are a disclosed sensitivity test, with no promised speedup.
stop_condition: Preserve failures and all measurements. No region/stride/direction/threshold adjustment or omitted slow trials. If context cropping matches speed, explicitly limit the novelty/performance claim; do not credit the regional API with inventing existing context selection.
split: Three existing, physically separate CT fields, all previously exposed research data. No labels or reserved final regions; software equivalence only, not fresh reading validation.
predecessors: E079 was a one-timing CPU demonstration against full inference and a naive context-dropping crop. It did not measure a careful context crop.

Global-grid/halo preservation already has the villa#1247 predecessor. A minimal aligned context crop can implement the same idea with the original Hecate runtime; this is the stronger competing explanation.
Existing Hecate fast-path and paired-feature optimizations are credited. This study does not compare GPU implementations or establish superiority over all optimized readers.
competing_explanations: Regional software preserves full-field results with repeatable time and temporary-storage savings.
The single-run speedup is unstable or the context-crop alternative provides the same compute reduction; the additional contribution is automation and smaller output accumulation.
Large regions need nearly all tiles, so a small-ROI speedup does not generalize to full-scroll reading.
scope: A stronger reproducibility test of existing software, not an ink-accuracy or new-text experiment.
environment: Fresh .venv-roi-review Python3.12.15, pinned existing dependencies from hashed wheels; no SciPy or workspace imports in the model worker.
operational: Require AC power and known-open lid before and during timed workers. Preserve partial artifacts and stop on a power/sleep/resource failure. A clean waiting-for-power state can resume; a failed worker cannot automatically retry.
